title: The adjustment set is a property of the scale
question: Does the set of covariates whose imbalance changes a transported contrast differ between the risk difference, risk ratio, marginal odds ratio and conditional odds ratio scales?
design: Population-level numerical study: logistic outcome with 0 to 3 conditional modifiers and 2 or 6 prognostic non-modifiers, two prognostic strengths and two imbalances; each covariate's omission scored by its relative change in the target contrast on four scales.
answer: The covariates a transported contrast depends on change with the scale, but not in the nested way DESIGN.md predicted. Prognostic non-modifiers never affected the conditional log odds ratio and affected some marginal scale by more than 5% in 13 of 24 scenarios, the risk difference included, because with a logistic model every prognostic variable modifies the risk difference; the risk difference was in fact the most sensitive scale (median 4.5% change per unbalanced prognostic variable, against 1.6% for the marginal odds ratio). Sets differed between the risk difference, marginal and conditional odds ratio in 10 of 24 scenarios, below the registered threshold of half, so the refuting sentence holds as registered.
findings: Registered verdict: refuting sentence HOLDS (sets differ in 42% of scenarios against a 50% threshold).
Marginal odds ratio set containing the risk-difference set (DESIGN.md's prediction): 19 of 24 scenarios.

Median relative change from one unbalanced prognostic variable: 0.045 (risk difference), 0.035 (log risk ratio), 0.016 (marginal log odds ratio), 0 (conditional log odds ratio). Near-null contrasts inflate relative changes.
not_answered: No time-to-event scale; no sampling or estimation of the sets; independent normal covariates. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Target A-versus-C contrast on the risk difference, log risk ratio, marginal and conditional log odds ratio scales
methods_compared: mean balancing with each covariate in turn left unbalanced
n_sim: Population-level calculation, 24 scenarios, 10^6 common random draws each
